title: Object-Relational Mapping
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of object-relational mapping in a C#/.NET program.
Predict the result of the included C# example and verify the documented output.
Apply object-relational mapping to a small task and identify one relevant boundary, limitation, or version requirement.

content.intro: Object-Relational Mapping is lesson 155 in APIs, Networking, and Database Integration. Integration code should isolate network or database calls, use parameters instead of string-built commands, validate external data, and define transaction boundaries.
content.why_it_matters: External systems fail and return untrusted data, so integration code needs timeouts, validation, and clear data boundaries. This lesson focuses on object-relational mapping and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small C# example that demonstrates object-relational mapping. Change one input or implementation detail, predict the result, then check it locally and explain one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates object-relational mapping rather than only repeating its definition.
The result is checked locally or against a clearly documented reference output.
At least one relevant boundary, invalid-input case, or compatibility condition is considered.
hints: List the assumptions and expected behavior for object-relational mapping before editing the code.
Change one variable or rule at a time; keep the previous output for comparison.
If behavior differs, confirm the compiler/target framework and consult the linked official documentation.
content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: identify the expected input and output, start from the smallest example, use the feature only where it clarifies the rule, and verify both a typical case and a boundary/failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the feature works identically on every target
common_mistakes.why: Language syntax, libraries, and runtime support are version-dependent.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the target framework and official versioned reference before using the feature.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary values, malformed input, and failure states often expose the real bug.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one typical input and one boundary or invalid case to the manual or automated checks.
